summary.text: A 54-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis diagnosed in 2013 had an MS attack with vertigo and nausea in 2019. MRI showed demyelinating lesions at the right lateral margin of the fourth ventricle, and negative Dix-Hallpike and Miniconi tests dismissed semicircular canal affection, so a central vestibular disorder was confirmed.

At the initial evaluation she reported severe dizziness with postural problems and a Dizziness Handicap Inventory score of 62; baseline Berg Balance Scale was 47 of 56 with inability to hold Romberg with closed eyes and tandem positions, and the Modified Fatigue Impact Scale was 61. Her MMSE was 25 of 30 with a memory impairment attributed to an MS attack, and her EDSS was 3.0 with ambulation preserved without a walking aid.

She completed a 20-session immersive virtual reality vestibular protocol of initial and advanced phases, two to three 50-minute sessions weekly for 7 weeks, at home with a supervising therapist, and was evaluated between phases, after the intervention and 1 month later.

Dizziness improved from a Dizziness Handicap Inventory score of 62 to 4 postintervention and 6 at 1 month, the Berg Balance Scale reached 54 and then 56, fatigue fell then rose again at 1 month, physical and mental quality of life improved, muscular tone trended lower, and she rated usability 90%.
